name: Geuel
overview: Geuel was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known primarily for being one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is his unique distinguishing feature in Scripture, highlighting his participation in a significant moment of Israelite history.
namesAndTitles: The name Geuel means 'splendor of G-d [El],' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 13:15, does not indicate that the name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful connection to divine splendor.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Geuel was the son of Machi, providing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Geuel's significance lies in his role as one of the twelve spies from the tribe of Gad, chosen to scout the Promised Land. This mission was critical in the unfolding of Israel's journey and God's plan for the nation. His inclusion among the spies underscores the tribal representation and collective responsibility in God's covenant community.
